findings.body: On the final retry of an ordinary runner error, `acknowledgeFailedTurn` is true even when no reply or failure notice was delivered. `handleFailure` then keeps the input consumed, so recovery cannot give the unanswered message to another turn. Release input whenever no output reached the user.
findings.title: Not done: No message is lost or given twice

findings.body: The follow-up is consumed under the `commandId` passed here, but `routeScopeActiveLiveTurnAdmission` drops that field when it calls `routeMessage` at lines 335–342. `LiveTurnAuthority.routeMessage` therefore generates a different command ID. If the runner rejects the continuation or finishes while it is pending, `releaseLiveContinuationCommand` releases by the appended command ID and matches no consumed item. The follow-up remains stranded. Forward `commandId` and `expectedTurnId` through the routing helper.
findings.title: Not done: No message is lost or given twice

findings.body: The spawned processes only call `takeInput` and `getMessagesByIds`, then exit. The active-turn follow-up case uses two worker objects in one process, a fake runner, and an IPC callback that merely records the write. It never proves that a real runner receives the follow-up and that replies across two processes leave no message dropped or doubled.
findings.title: Not done: two-process no-loss/no-duplication test

findings.body: The restart message test constructs claimed turns and injects a fake runner in an integration test. The real-runner end-to-end case exercises a successful turn and settings reload, but no crashed worker recovery. There is no end-to-end proof through the real turn entry point that restart delivers unanswered input while leaving answered input consumed.
findings.title: Not done: restart recovery end-to-end test

findings.body: The added before- and after-output cases invoke `app.processGroupMessages` with an injected runner. The real-runner end-to-end case covers success only. The required test still needs to drive the spawned runner and delivery path through failures on both sides of output, then assert which input the next turn receives.
findings.title: Not done: failure before/after output end-to-end test

findings.body: The integration failure case retries without `finalRetry`; the final-retry tests cover a provider failure notice instead. No test drives an ordinary final retry that fails without delivering output and verifies that a later turn receives its input. That case would expose the consumption loss at `group-processing.ts:763`.
findings.title: Not done: final-retry failure before output test
